title: Subject
description:
One thing that can be classified, in one file. Identified by a URN of the form <namespace>:<path>, resolvable without knowing what wrote it.

This document is FLAT: every value is a scalar or a list of scalars, and nothing nests. That is a deliberate constraint on the format rather than a limitation of it. A collection document holding many subjects needed a list of mappings, which no thirty-line reader in another language will implement correctly, and which the store's own reader could not read back. Flat front matter can be read by anything. See ledger/0002.

id.description: The URN. 'psmodule:PSModuleGraph/function/Get-PSModuleClass' and 'facet:networking' are both valid; the second is how a facet becomes classifiable by another facet.

namespace.description: The URN's scheme. The set of namespaces is DATA, not an enum in code. See NAMING.md.

name.description: Human-readable label. Not an identifier and not required to be unique.

parent.description: Containing subject, when there is one. A function's parent is its module.

source.description: Where the subject was observed. Repository-relative, never absolute: an absolute path leaks a username into a file meant to travel.

aliases.description: Former identifiers that still resolve. A rename never deletes.

generated_by.description: What produced this file, so a reader can tell asserted data from derived data.

prompt.description: Ledger entry that produced this file.
